reason: Both cover the same facets (RAS core, renal sodium/volume handling, aldosterone, vasopressin-water, vasoconstriction/NO-cGMP smooth muscle), but B spreads them over 40 heavily overlapping themes and adds junk such as insemination, peristalsis and parturition, while A delivers them in 16 cleaner themes.

A's 9 themes cleanly separate docking/SNARE, neurotransmitter release cycles, Ca2+-dependent exocytosis/short-term plasticity, vesicle recycling and presynaptic Ca2+-channel modulation, whereas B repeats these in 21 near-duplicate themes with only a minor cholinergic/NMJ and postsynaptic addition.

A covers ERBB adaptor signalling, receptor endocytic downregulation, PTK6, MET crosstalk and the broad RTK/MAPK level in 11 themes, while B repeats these across 26 overlapping themes and pads them with weakly related PDGF/YAP-TAZ fibroblast modules; its ERBB2 mutant/drug-resistance theme does not outweigh the clutter.

B covers the key contexts (TLS polymerases, polymerase switching at the fork, NER and BER gap filling, UV damage, telomere C-strand, somatic hypermutation, broad genome maintenance) in 12 themes, whereas A spreads the same contexts over 23 heavily redundant themes; A's extra mid-level DSB/fork-reversal theme is only a small gain.

B lays out the DISC/c-FLIP core, extrinsic apoptosis, necroptosis, T-cell AICD, pyroptosis/inflammasome, mitochondrial apoptosis and p53/senescence in 12 distinct themes, while A has 27 themes that mostly reshuffle the same members; A's TNFR1/LUBAC themes are the only real facet B lacks.

B covers snRNA transcription, core spliceosome/tri-snRNP, Pol III, nuclear exosome decay, mRNA 3'-end/export, rRNA/MYC and mitochondrial RNA in 18 themes, while A has 37 themes that repeat these and drift into OXPHOS, translation initiation and miRNA decay contexts unrelated to tri-snRNP assembly.
